title: Add profiling baselines, representative workload runners, and reporting pipeline v22
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Improve our benchmark lab coverage for common RLHF-style and document-summarization workloads, establish profiling baselines for cold and steady-state runs, and wire a lightweight reporting pipeline so results are centrally available in the observability stack. This PR bundles three changes: (1) representative workload runners for dialog, summarization and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), (2) profiling baseline scripts + canonical config for cold/steady-state runs, and (3) a reporting pipeline that publishes summarized metrics to the benchmark reports S3 bucket and to the internal Grafana datasource.

Summary of changes: added new runners under benchmark-lab/runners/, a profiling baseline suite under benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines/, pipeline manifests under benchmark-lab/pipeline/ and a CI job to run nightly baselines (ci/benchmark-lab-nightly.yml). Updated docs/benchmark-lab.md with usage and interpretation guidance.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement dialog, summarization and rag runners (simple, reproducible configs).
- [x] Add profiling harness and canonical seed/config for repeatability.
- [x] Add lightweight reporting pipeline (YAML manifests + reporting lambda).
- [x] Add nightly CI job and alert on regression.
- [x] Docs and runbook updates.

Testing: Local unit tests added for runner config parsing (benchmark-lab/tests/test_runners.py). End-to-end smoke tested on internal dev cluster using a small MPT-7B compatible variant; profiling baselines reproduce previous median latencies within 5%. Nightly CI job was run in staging and completed successfully (see CI checks).

Rollout plan: Merge to main. Nightly job triggers in staging for 48h; if no regressions, promote to production schedule. Rollback: disable nightly CI job and revert pipeline manifest; previous reporting consumer ignores unknown job ids.

Notes: Kept runners intentionally small and opinionated to avoid coupling with serving runtime scheduling heuristics. Larger perf experiments will live in perf-canary repo as follow-ups.

References: Linear ENG-4321, PERF-1182. Related PRs: pr-56042 (cold-start-profiling), pr-53421 (profiling baselines v20).
